# Bike Stories

> A private maintenance log for every bike you own: services and when the next one is due, parts and how worn they are, rides from Apple Health or GPX, receipts and manuals — plus what each bike actually costs, per kilometre. Free on iPhone; Pro is a one-time $9.99 unlock.

Bike Stories is an iPhone app that keeps the whole story of every bike you own. It tracks maintenance schedules and service history, parts and their wear, rides (logged by hand, imported from Apple Health, or loaded from a GPX file), expenses, documents and photos — and rolls purchase price, parts and servicing into a total cost of ownership with a cost-per-kilometre figure. There is no account: data lives on the device and syncs through the user's own iCloud. It is a logbook, not a social or training platform — there are no leaderboards, no feed and no community.

## Key Facts

- Platform: iOS (iPhone, iOS 17+)
- Pricing: free to download and free for up to 2 bikes with every logging feature. "Bike Stories Pro" is a one-time $9.99 in-app purchase — unlimited bikes, Apple Health ride import, PDF export, automatic backups. No subscription, no ads
- Storage: local SwiftData store on the device, shared with the widget and share extension, mirrored to the user's own private iCloud (CloudKit). No Bike Stories server holds user data
- Privacy: no account, no sign-up, no email. Anonymous usage analytics including session replay go to PostHog (EU) and can be switched off in Settings; bike data is never sent — see https://bike-stories.12f.dk/privacy-policy.html. Nothing is sold
- Units: kilometres or miles, and the user's own currency, both locale-aware
- Languages: 49
- Developer: 12F ApS, Denmark (https://12f.dk/)
- Website: https://bike-stories.12f.dk/
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/bike-stories-maintenance-log/id6783374730

## Features

- Multi-bike "Garage": 13 bike types (road, mountain, gravel, hybrid, city, electric, cargo, folding, touring, cyclocross, BMX, kids, other), each with its own history
- Starter templates: pick the kind of bike you ride and it arrives with a maintenance schedule already in place
- Cost of ownership per bike: purchase + parts + maintenance + expenses, with a colour-coded breakdown and cost per kilometre or mile
- Maintenance scheduled by date, by distance, or both, with 10 preset service types and a full service history including costs
- Local notifications when a service falls due, and before a document (insurance, registration) expires
- Parts across 13 categories with brand, model, price and wear tracking shown as a life-remaining bar
- Spares and stock inventory, deducted automatically when a part is fitted
- Rides: manual entry, Apple Health cycling-workout import (manual or automatic, Pro), and GPX import with the route drawn on a map
- Per-bike odometer built from logged rides, plus a 12-week activity chart on each bike card
- Documents: manuals, receipts, warranties, insurance and registration, with renewal reminders
- Photo galleries per bike and per ride, plus a share extension to file a photo or PDF from another app
- Insights: distance per month, riding by weekday, spending over time, total spend and cost per distance
- E-bike battery health checks: measured capacity, estimated range and charge cycles over time
- Tyre pressure log (front and rear, charted) and a reference setup sheet for pressures, suspension and saddle height
- Home-screen widget mirroring a bike's odometer, distance this month and next service
- iCloud sync across the owner's devices; PDF export of the service history and a seller document (Pro); automatic local backups (Pro)
- Dark mode, Dynamic Type and VoiceOver support; status is never conveyed by colour alone

## What Bike Stories deliberately does not have

- No account, sign-up or login
- No subscription — Pro is bought once
- No ads, and no shop, brand or insurer can pay for placement
- No social feed, leaderboards, segments or training plans — it is a logbook, not a training platform
- No server of ours holding your bikes; nothing is sold to anyone

## Blog

The Bike Stories blog publishes practical bicycle maintenance guidance — what wears out and when, how to keep a service history, and what a bike really costs to run — at https://bike-stories.12f.dk/blog/ (RSS feed: https://bike-stories.12f.dk/feed.xml). Posts are tagged `maintenance`, `parts-and-wear`, `costs`, `riding` or `kids`.

### When to replace a bike chain (and what it costs if you don't) (2026-08-27, parts-and-wear)
https://bike-stories.12f.dk/blog/when-to-replace-a-bike-chain/
A practical guide to bicycle chain wear: what "stretch" really means (pin and bushing wear, not metal stretching), how to measure it with a chain checker or a steel ruler, the 0.5% and 0.75% thresholds and which applies to your drivetrain, realistic mileage ranges by riding conditions, and the arithmetic of why replacing a chain on time is the cheapest maintenance decision on the bike. Includes what to do when you have already left it too late.

### What size bike a kid actually needs — inseam and standover, not age (2026-08-27, kids)
https://bike-stories.12f.dk/blog/what-size-bike-a-kid-actually-needs/
A practical sizing guide for choosing a child's bike using measurement instead of age. Covers how to measure a child's inseam, the standover height check, why the brake-lever reach test matters more than wheel size for safety, and why buying a frame too large to 'grow into' is a genuine safety problem. Includes a worked example for a 5-year-old and the weight consideration that most parents never check. Explicitly separates advice for a balance-bike user from advice for a geared 24-inch user.

## How it works, in detail

1. **Add a bike.** Tap one of the starter templates — the kind of bike you ride — and Bike Stories creates the bike with a maintenance schedule that suits it (a city bike and a full-suspension mountain bike do not need the same services). Or fill in the form yourself: name, type, brand, model, purchase date and price, and the odometer reading you are starting from.
2. **Log rides.** Three routes in: type a ride by hand (distance, date, duration, optional notes); import cycling workouts from Apple Health, either on demand or automatically as they appear (Pro); or load a GPX file, which also draws the route on a map. Every ride belongs to one bike and can be moved to another if it was filed wrongly.
3. **Log parts and services.** A part carries a category, brand, model, price, fitted date and an optional expected life. When it has an expected life, Bike Stories counts the distance ridden since it was fitted and shows the remaining life as a bar plus a percentage. A maintenance record carries a date, a type, a cost and notes, and a schedule can make the next one due by date, by distance, or both.
4. **Store the paperwork.** Manuals, receipts, warranties, insurance and registration documents are attached to the bike. Those with an expiry date get a renewal reminder.
5. **Read the numbers.** Each bike's dashboard shows total distance as a hero metric with total cost, cost per kilometre or mile, part count and next service in a stat grid beneath it. The cost breakdown splits the total into purchase, parts, maintenance and expenses. Insights charts distance per month, riding by weekday and spending over time.

## Who it is for

- Daily commuters, whose consumables wear out on a distance-based schedule
- Home mechanics who already think in chain-wear numbers and want somewhere to keep them
- E-bike owners tracking battery capacity, range and cycles as the pack ages
- Riders with several bikes, each needing its own history and service intervals
- Families managing a fleet, including kids' bikes that get outgrown
- Anyone about to sell a bike, who wants a dated service history to hand to the buyer

## Accuracy and limitations

- Bike Stories records what you tell it. Wear percentages are derived from the expected life you set and the distance logged since fitting — they are a planning aid, not a measurement of chain elongation or pad thickness. Check the part.
- Apple Health import depends on other apps writing cycling workouts to Health. If an app does not write there, or you have not granted it permission, those rides will not appear.
- The odometer reflects rides that have been logged. A ride that was never recorded anywhere will not be counted.
- Costs are recorded in the currency you choose in Settings; the app does not convert between currencies or track resale value automatically.
- It is a logbook, not a training platform: there is no power analysis, no training load, no segments and no social feed.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is Bike Stories free?

The app is free to download and free to use for up to two bikes, with every logging feature included: maintenance, parts, rides, costs, documents and photos. Bike Stories Pro is a one-time $9.99 in-app unlock that removes the bike limit and adds Apple Health ride import, PDF export and automatic backups. There is no subscription.

### Do I need an account?

No. There is no sign-up, no email and no Bike Stories server holding your data. Your bikes live on your iPhone and sync between your own devices through your iCloud account, which only you can read.

### Can it import my rides automatically?

Yes. Bike Stories reads cycling workouts from Apple Health, so anything that writes there — your watch, Strava, Wahoo, Garmin Connect and the rest, when you let them — can become a ride on the right bike. Turn on automatic sync and new workouts are picked up when you open the app. You can also load a GPX file and see the route on a map, or log a ride by hand. Health import is part of Pro; manual rides and GPX are free.

### Does it work for e-bikes and mountain bikes?

Yes — there are 13 bike types, from road and gravel to mountain, city, cargo, folding and electric, and each starter template comes with a maintenance schedule that suits it. E-bikes also get battery health checks: measured capacity, estimated range and charge cycles, tracked over time.

### How does it know when a service is due?

You schedule a service by date, by distance, or both — every 500 km, or every six months, whichever comes first. The bike's odometer builds itself from the rides you log, so a distance-based service becomes due as you ride. With reminders switched on, a notification arrives when something falls due.

### What happens to my data?

It stays yours. Bikes, rides, receipts and photos are stored on your device and mirrored to your own iCloud account — nothing is uploaded to us and nothing is sold. The app does send anonymous, non-identifying usage analytics, including session replay of the interface, so we can see which screens people get stuck on; no bike data is ever included, and you can switch it off in Settings → Privacy. The details are at https://bike-stories.12f.dk/privacy-policy.html.

### Can I get my data out again?

Yes. Pro exports a bike's service and cost history as a PDF, plus a seller document for when you sell the bike. Pro also keeps automatic local backups you can restore from.

### What do I need to run it?

An iPhone running iOS 17 or later. No account, no subscription and no internet connection to read your own logbook. Distances show in kilometres or miles and costs in your own currency, and the app is available in 49 languages.
